source.citation: Atlas of Pidgin and Creole Language Structures survey of Cameroon Pidgin English, and a University of Reunion paper on whether to teach it. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: An English-based pidgin that serves as a language of wider communication across Cameroon.
attributes.status: Less prestigious than English and French, but felt to be more African than either. It has no official status.
attributes.regional_languages: About 7 or 8 indigenous languages and Cameroon Pidgin English have become regional lingua francas.
attributes.speakers: The number of speakers is hard to determine because they range from first-language and fluent second-language speakers to people who use it only occasionally.
attributes.grammar_note: Nouns do not change for number or gender.
attributes.old_data: A 1983 study found Pidgin as a first language for 22% of the people in Bamenda, 25% in Mamfe, 19% in Kumba, 26% in Buea and 31% in Limbe.
